title: The Sun You See Is 8 Minutes Old
tts: TTS unavailable (ClientConnectorDNSError: Cannot connect to host speech.platform.bing.com:443 ssl:<ssl.SSLContext object at 0x7f0456) -> silent render + narration files for CapCut

lines.text: The Sun you see right now is eight minutes old.
lines.visual: kinetic: The Sun you see | right now is | *8 minutes* old

lines.text: Light is the fastest thing there is, about three hundred thousand kilometers every second.
lines.visual: stat: label=Speed of light | from=0 | to=299792 | suffix= km/s | sub=Fast enough to circle the Earth seven times in one second

lines.text: But the Sun is one hundred fifty million kilometers away, so the trip takes eight minutes and nineteen seconds.
lines.visual: lightbeam: title=Sunlight's trip | from=Sun | to=Earth | time=8:19 | distance=149.6 million km

lines.text: If the Sun vanished right now, we would keep seeing it shine for eight more minutes.
Sunlight takes forty three minutes to reach Jupiter, and over four hours to reach Neptune.
lines.visual: lightscale: Earth@8.3 min | Mars@12.7 min | Jupiter@43 min | Neptune@4.2 hours | title=Sunlight travel time | note=Spacing not to scale

lines.text: And it has a lot to light up. A hundred and nine Earths fit across the Sun.
So tonight, look up. You are seeing the past.
lines.visual: kinetic: Look up. | You are seeing | the *past*.
